chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'The traveler who does not settle in his home town for five days or less shortens his prayer during the day and completes it at night, and upon him is the fasting of the month of Ramadan. But if he has a residence in the town he goes to for ten days or more, he shortens his prayer and breaks his fast (does not fast).'

key_terms.أَتَمَّ: Completed (referring to the full duration of prayer or fasting)
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: The traveler (one who travels for trade or business)
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan
key_terms.قَصَّرَ: Shortened (referring to the four-rak'ah prayer reduced to two)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer and fasting for a traveler staying in a place for less than ten days?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the threshold for changing travel status, specifying that a stay of ten days or more renders one a resident (*muqim*) subject to full prayers and fasting, while shorter stays maintain traveler privileges. It highlights the practical application of the 'ten-day rule' in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between temporary sojourns and established residence based on the duration of stay in a single location.
